answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a meaningful stake that is slashed if peers reject its work. A flood of fakes would have to split one budget across thousands of identities, each too small to influence anything. Staking spreads that cost across a nebula of small commitments that collectively secure the network, while each agent's public key serves as a cipher proving who actually put value at risk. Reputation then settles into a crystal: brittle to cheats, transparent to everyone auditing who is real.
